questions.q: What will Yahweh do when people ask him for rain?
questions.a: Yahweh will give them rain showers, and he will make plants grow in the field.

questions.q: What causes the people to wander like sheep and suffer?
questions.a: The people wander like sheep and suffer because the household idols speak falsely, the diviners envision a lie, they tell empty dreams, and they give empty comfort. The people also have no shepherd.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh say he will punish?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will punish the leaders, whom he calls the male goats.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will come from the house of Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh says the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow, and every ruler will come from the house of Judah.

questions.q: What will the people’s warriors do because Yahweh is with them?
questions.a: They will fight like warriors trampling their enemies in the mud of the streets, and they will defeat the horsemen because Yahweh is with them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do for the house of Judah and the house of Joseph?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would strengthen the house of Judah, save the house of Joseph, bring them back, and have compassion on them.

questions.q: How will the people of Ephraim feel because of what Yahweh has done?
questions.a: The people of Ephraim will be glad like warriors who have drunk wine, and their children will see it and rejoice in Yahweh.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do because he has redeemed his people?
questions.a: Yahweh will whistle for his people and gather them together, and they will become as many as they were before.

questions.q: What will Judah and Ephraim do when they remember Yahweh in the distant countries where Yahweh has scattered them?
questions.a: They and their children will live and return when they remember Yahweh in the distant countries where he has scattered them.

questions.q: Where will Yahweh gather his people from, and where will he bring them?
questions.a: Yahweh will gather his people from Egypt and Assyria, and he will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, where there will not be enough room for them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to Assyria and Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would bring down the pride of Assyria and take away the scepter of Egypt.

questions.q: How will the people live after Yahweh strengthens them?
questions.a: The people will live faithfully, honoring Yahweh’s name.

commentary.text: Blessings to be sought from the Lord.

Verses 1–5 Spiritual blessings had been promised under figurative allusions to earthly plenty. Seasonable rain is a great mercy, which we may ask of God when there is most need of it, and we may look for it to come. We must in our prayers ask for mercies in their proper time. The Lord would make bright clouds, and give showers of rain. This may be an exhortation to seek the influences of the Holy Spirit, in faith and by prayer, through which the blessings held forth in the promises are obtained and enjoyed. The prophet shows the folly of making addresses to idols, as their fathers had done. The Lord visited the remnant of his flock in mercy, and was about to renew their courage and strength for conflict and victory. Every creature is to us what God makes it to be. Every one raised to support the nation, as a corner-stone does the building, or to unite those that differ, as nails join the different timbers, must come from the Lord; and those employed to overcome their enemies, must have strength and success from him. This may be applied to Christ; to him we must look to raise up persons to unite, support, and defend his people. He never will say, Seek ye me in vain.

Here are precious promises to the people of God, which look to the state of the Jews, and even to the latter days of the church. Preaching the gospel is God's call for souls to come to Jesus Christ. Those whom Christ redeemed by his blood, God will gather by his grace. Difficulties shall be got over easily, and effectually, as those in the way of the deliverance out of Egypt. God himself will be their strength, and their song. When we resist, and so overcome our spiritual enemies, then our hearts shall rejoice. If God strengthen us, we must bestir ourselves in all the duties of the Christian life, must be active in the work of God; and we must do all in the name of the Lord Jesus.
